intervention.title: Fix compaction so important information survives
intervention.summary: Change the compaction instructions or implementation to preserve information that later work needs. Where the harness allows it, compare changes on a saved conversation before evaluating ordinary future work.

purpose.p: Improve what the compactor keeps so critical information is not forgotten. A completed action may still carry a decision, a failed approach, or a permission limit that future work needs. Choose what to preserve by its likely use, not just by whether the action is finished.

precondition.title: Important information was lost
precondition.p: Important information disappears during compaction, as proposed in incorrect compaction. Repeated retrieval, lost constraints, or repeated permission requests can point you toward an incident to inspect.

precondition.title: A supported way to influence compaction
precondition.p: The harness exposes compaction instructions, a hook, or an implementation you control. Identify which path the installed version actually uses. A general instructions file is not automatically a compaction prompt. If the provider hides the retained state, use subsequent behavior to assess the change and record that you cannot inspect the summary directly.

step.title: Find the control that applies
step.p: Use the harness notes below to locate the relevant setting or hook, then save its current version. Compare the affected conversation with the summary or first subsequent mistake. Identify the missing information and why later work needed it.

step.title: Save the conversation before compaction
step.p: Reuse existing session records. If an upcoming compaction would lose needed evidence, capture it with a supported hook or export. Keep an unchanged copy for comparison and save the resulting summary when it is readable. Agree with the user where these private records go and how long to keep them.

step.title: Change what compaction preserves
step.p: Make a small change tied to the observed omission. For example, if permission survived but its scope did not, ask the compactor to retain each permission together with its limits and expiry conditions. Inspect the existing instructions before adding another rule. Do not remove completed work indiscriminately or hard-code the answer from one incident into the prompt.

step.title: Compare on a frozen conversation when practical
step.p: If the harness can fork or replay the saved conversation from before compaction, give the original and revised compactor the same input. Start each candidate from that unchanged input, not from the previous candidate's summary. Keep the model, settings, and relevant instruction files fixed apart from the intended change.

Compare whether the needed facts and their qualifications survive, what else is lost, and how much space is used. A small number of focused revisions can be faster than waiting for new incidents. This holds the input steady; it does not make model output deterministic. Stop when further trials are unlikely to change the decision.

step.title: Check what survived and deploy the change
step.p: Inspect the retained state where possible. If it is opaque, a short continuation with external actions disabled can test whether the agent still follows the relevant constraint; it cannot prove which facts are encoded. A readable summary that looks right is also not enough by itself. Confirm the selected change reaches future sessions.

step.title: Review occasional samples
step.p: Review occasional saved compactions and the work that followed them, using an existing background job where practical. Check a few different kinds of task so a fix for one conversation does not silently damage another. Avoid extra checking on every working turn.

step.title: Agree on a check-in date
step.p: Agree with the user on a check-in date, who will review the samples, and a reminder or scheduled job. For example, review in three workdays if normal use should produce several compactions; if too few occur, report that and choose another date.

harness.title: Claude Code
harness.p: Customize: Claude Code documents a Compact Instructions section in CLAUDE.md for persistent compaction guidance. Use /compact with a focus instruction for a single comparison. This is the documented route; there is no need to invent a separate compaction AGENTS.md. See context management.

Capture: The PreCompact hook receives transcript_path; PostCompact receives compact_summary. Use these to save the before-and-after evidence. PostCompact cannot rewrite the result; logging a summary and changing compaction are separate operations. Check hook support in the installed version.

Compare: Preserve a session from before compaction, then use claude --resume SESSION_ID --fork-session for each candidate and run /compact with the candidate focus. The fork flag gives the continuation a new session ID. Forking an already compacted session does not recreate its original input. Test the final persistent CLAUDE.md change as well as any temporary focus instruction.

harness.title: Codex CLI
harness.p: Customize: The configuration reference documents compact_prompt for an inline override and experimental_compact_prompt_file for a file-based override. These are compaction-specific settings; ordinary AGENTS.md guidance should not be treated as a replacement prompt. Check that the installed version and compaction path honor the override before assessing its effect.

Compare: Keep an untouched session from before compaction. Use codex fork SESSION_ID for a separate candidate session, then /compact. The command reference also documents /export for a readable conversation record. A Markdown export is evidence for review, not a promised exact replay format. Use saved sessions for forks and confirm the effective configuration in each one.

Limit: Provider-side compaction can return an opaque state rather than a readable summary. Do not assume a local prompt setting controls every such path. When the state cannot be inspected, compare a constrained continuation and record that limitation. These notes cover the CLI; verify the controls separately for hosted Codex surfaces.

harness.title: OpenCode
harness.p: Customize: In the V1 plugin API, experimental.session.compacting can append guidance through output.context or replace the prompt through output.prompt. A replacement ignores the context array, so preserve the useful parts of the default prompt deliberately. AGENTS.md supplies general project instructions; the hook is the explicit compaction control.

Compare: V1 documents opencode --session SESSION_ID --fork, opencode export SESSION_ID, and /compact. Fork the same saved session before each candidate compaction and keep the export privately. See the CLI and TUI references.

Version matters: The V2 migration guide replaces the V1 hook with ctx.session.hook("compaction", ...); V1 plugin implementations do not run unchanged in V2. Use the API for the version deployed in your system.

harness.title: Custom harness
harness.p: Customize and compare: If you own the summarizer, save its exact input, system instructions, model settings, and output format. Run only that summarization step against the frozen input while changing the targeted instruction. Keep external tools out of the comparison. Then test the chosen change on a separate incident and in ordinary future work.

Opaque compaction: OpenAI's Responses compaction API returns a compacted window containing an encrypted item. Keep the returned window intact for subsequent requests; it is not a text summary to edit or inspect. A custom summarizer experiment does not establish how that provider-managed path behaves.

ul.li: Before applying the change, record which lost facts should now survive and which later mistakes should decline. Use the predictions in D001 when that explanation fits.

Use a frozen-input comparison, when available, to reject poor candidates quickly. Keep an untouched incident for a separate check. A better summary on the example used to tune the prompt is preliminary evidence, not proof of a lasting repair.
At the agreed check-in, compare retained information and subsequent work. Did requirements and permission limits survive? Did the agent repeat less work? Was enough context space still available?
If the facts survive but mistakes continue, reconsider the explanation. If evidence was not captured or no relevant compaction occurred, say that the review is inconclusive.

Keeping too much can fill the context; keeping outdated facts can cause bad decisions. A summary can also preserve permission while dropping its limits. Removing completed work can erase why an approach failed.
Saved conversations can contain private data. Keep collection limited to the agreed location and retention period. A model, harness, or task change can make comparisons harder.

Forking a conversation does not necessarily isolate its files, credentials, or external services. A continuation test must not repeat the original task's external actions. Prompt revisions can overfit a single transcript.
Restore the previous compaction instructions or implementation if the change causes stale decisions, lost permission limits, or excessive context use.
Correct affected summaries and repair any resulting work. Reverting the prompt does not undo actions already taken.
Remove temporary capture or review hooks when the agreed review ends, unless the user chooses to keep them.
